newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FREEING OF SOUTH AFRICAN FARM TRADE SEEN ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: FREEING OF SOUTH AFRICAN FARM TRADE SEEN ON TRACK.

text.p: The council in charge of scrapping South Africa's statutory farm product control boards said on Friday the process should be close to complete by the January deadline.

"The Act stipulates that all the control boards ought to have been deregulated, and the schemes repealed, or in the process of being repealed, by January 1998," Eckart Kassier, chairman of the National Agricultural Marketing Council, told a parliamentary committee.
"The act does give the possibility of extension, but we still hope to reach that objective," he said. "It may be that in certain cases we have to ask for an extension."
Kassier said his council, which began work in January, had received very good cooperation from most of the 14 control boards, but "certainly not all".

"We have progressed fairly well up to now," said Kassier, adding that at least half the boards had submitted business plans spelling out what they would do with their funds and what kinds of structures they envisaged taking over their functions.
Plans had been submitted by the boards regulating maize, oilseeds, lucerne, potatoes, dried beans, meat and sorghum.
Kassier said control boards had done a good job of compiling information databases, and these should not be lost.

"So the imposition of statutory levies for information generation seems to be favoured across the board by all directly affected groups," he said, adding that levies to pay for research had also received support.
